plainText:
Junichi Masuda (Japanese: Masuda Jun'ichi, born January 12, 1968 in Yokohama) is one of the directors and music composers of Game Freak and the current Chief Creative Fellow at The Pokémon Company. He has served as the game director of multiple Pokémon games.

From 2004 through 2015, Masuda posted to the Director's Columns blog on Game Freak's website, with many of the entries translated into English. These entries explained the reasoning behind his creative decisions in the Pokémon franchise and presented updates about games during development. It was through this column that the Masuda method, a method of obtaining Shiny Pokémon more easily, was first documented. On March 31, 2016, Masuda migrated to LINE BLOG, and posted there through 2017.

==Early life and career==
Masuda was born in the , located in the real-life , on January 12, 1968. His family would vacation in the , which became the basis for the Pokémon world's Hoenn. As a teenager, he played the trombone and had an interest in classical music, while also maintaining an interest in arcade games and their programming. After high school, Masuda attended Japan Electronics College, where he studied Computer Graphics, though he was still interested in music as a hobby. He was working in a corporate office in 1989 when Satoshi Tajiri approached him and asked if he would like to join Game Freak, which was just beginning to form at the time. Masuda agreed and became one of the founding members of the company.

The first game that Masuda worked on with Game Freak was composing the music for , which was released in 1990. He also composed for Nintendo's in 1993 and 's in 1994. He also co-produced the Game Freak title .

==Musical influences==
While in elementary school, Masuda listened to the soundtracks of and , which he would attempt to emulate on his recorder. At the age of 9, Masuda received a cassette player from his parents, which he used to listen to rock and roll music. In junior high school, he became interested in , and was inspired by their use of synthesizers to ask his parents for his first synthesizer, a . He used the synthesizer to copy techno music he liked, including YMO, , and . Masuda also played games on Nintendo platforms and enjoyed the soundtracks of games including and , though he does not claim video game music as an influence. 

Masuda's favorite genre of music is techno; other techno bands he enjoys include , , and . He also enjoys the rock bands , , and .

==In the games==
 
 
===Generation VI===
Masuda made his first cameo appearance in the series in as the owner of a special Super-Secret Base in Mossdeep City that the player can visit after scanning a QR Code, which was first revealed in the Pokémon Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire Full Story Guide Book. The player can choose to challenge him and any of the three Grunts in his base to a Single Battle or invite him to their own Super-Secret Base. In battle, he uses three Cosplay Pikachu.

His team name is Team .
 
 
 
 
 
===Generation VIII===
Masuda appears in in the northwesternmost house in Hotel Grand Lake alongside one of his favorite Pokémon, . He evaluates the player's Pokédex and gives them a Diploma both for completing the Sinnoh Pokédex and for completing the National Pokédex. Along with Yuichi Ueda, he is only referred to in-game as "Game Director".

==Trivia==
In an interview with in December 2014, Masuda stated that he didn't originally work in as he was working on another project; however, he was brought back when the team faced issues during development. Whereas he worked as a programmer and composer in , in Gold and Silver, he worked on the audio and game design as well as in the coordination of the American and European localizations.
Masuda listens to and . He says that he is most inspired by the classical music composer . , , , and . 
Masuda's favorite move is , and his favorite type is the type. 
The character 's Japanese and optional English name Jun could be a reference to Masuda.
In the in , there is a named Masuda.
The character Vincent's Japanese name is Jun'ichi, another possible reference.
In the Generation II games and HeartGold and SoulSilver, there's another Guitarist in the Vermilion Gym named Jun'ichi and Vincent in Japanese and English respectively.
An NPC in Sootopolis City, Kiri, was named after Masuda's daughter, born right before the Japanese release of . 
Although the game did not get an official soundtrack release, Masuda is listed under "Music" in the credits of Pokémon Brilliant Diamond and Shining Pearl despite Shota Kageyama being known to have arranged the entirety of 's soundtrack for the remakes, including the composition of both Ramanas Park battle themes. 
Composers from the original Pokémon Diamond and Pearl soundtrack such as Hitomi Sato or Go Ichinose are not credited in any capacity, suggesting that the "Music" credits only include those that provided new work on the remakes. It is possible that this refers to the two unused tracks in Pokémon Brilliant Diamond and Shining Pearl, which both sound compositionally similar to Masuda's work for Pokémon GO.
According to some information in the Pokémon Omega Ruby & Pokémon Alpha Sapphire: Super Music Collection, Masuda's favorite song in the original Pokémon Ruby & Sapphire is the main theme that plays on the title screen, which he composed.
The concept for the Global Terminal was Masuda's idea.
